[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Memory Optimization and Dtype Selection in Pandas"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When working with large datasets in Pandas, memory consumption can quickly become a bottleneck, often leading to out-of-memory errors. By default, Pandas infers data types that are safe and general, such as 64-bit integers and floats, which consume more RAM than necessary. Optimizing data types (dtypes) is one of the most effective ways to reduce memory footprint and speed up data processing."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Default Memory Allocation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pandas assigns 64-bit precision to integers and floats by default (int64 and float64), and treats text columns as object data types. You can inspect the memory usage of a DataFrame using the info method with memory_usage='deep'."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Create a sample DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'id': range(100000),
    'value': np.random.randn(100000),
    'category': ['A'] * 50000 + ['B'] * 50000
})

print(df.info(memory_usage='deep'))"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Strategies for Downcasting Numeric Types"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Downcasting involves converting numeric columns to the smallest possible integer or float subtype that can safely hold the data without overflow. Pandas provides a built-in utility function called pd.to_numeric with the downcast parameter, or you can use the select_dtypes method combined with astype."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Downcasting integer columns
df['id'] = pd.to_numeric(df['id'], downcast='integer')

# Downcasting float columns
df['value'] = pd.to_numeric(df['value'], downcast='float')

print(df.dtypes)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Utilizing Categorical Dtypes"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"String columns stored as object types consume significant memory because Pandas stores pointers to Python objects. If a string column has a limited set of repeated values (low cardinality), converting it to the category dtype drastically reduces memory usage by storing integers internally instead of duplicate strings."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Convert category column to categorical dtype
df['category'] = df['category'].astype('category')

print(df.info(memory_usage='deep'))"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Loading Data"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Specify dtypes upfront: Use the dtype parameter in pd.read_csv() to define types during ingestion rather than modifying them afterward."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Process in chunks: If the dataset is larger than available RAM, use the chunksize parameter to process the file iteratively."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid object types: Regularly audit columns with object dtype and convert them to numeric, datetime, or categorical types."}]
